next_unit_hint: A boundary paragraph can only assert: per-case rows ship for all five arms + the decider and the per-K table reproduces identically across all four packages; the encoder loses at every K in 2..5; the gap is non-monotone in K (widest at K=3, narrowest at K=2) with the K=2 contrast being the only clean one (n=33, Wilson CI +/-0.16); encoders fall below the majority-class control only at K>=3; both arms are per-case named-option scorers with only 15 of 215 fixture option labels shared with the 34-label training corpus; encoder arms are order-equivariant (0/190 flips) while the majority control is not (58/190) and the decider has no order probe. It must NOT assert any data-scale effect (no data-fraction arm exists), anything about K>5 or fixed label spaces, or decider order-insensitivity. A learning-curve sweep is the decisive test for data scale; the harness (12 files) and data (train.jsonl 800 rows / dev.jsonl 200) exist locally at repro/encoder-crossover-190/harness/, but there is no GPU (nvidia-smi fails), no checkpoint anywhere, and MANIFEST.json:3 records 'all model weights withheld' - so it is re-training a model, not re-analysis. Any unit that quotes the harness as available must also note AVAILABILITY.md:24,43-44 declares it withheld.
